thread:
omar: Heads-up — want to align on scope for the FlashAttention v2->v3 integration. I'm proposing a phased migration that covers kernel selection logic, batching heuristics, and KV cache interaction checks.

jin: +1. can we spell out the heuristics first? last perf run showed weird regressions at seq_len 4096 with small batch sizes.

sarah: Noted. My profiling showed v3 uses a different tiling strategy; latency variance spikes when KV pages are touched. I’ll paste the flamegraph link after i upload.

mike: Important: we should gate v3 behind a feature flag per-cluster and also add an automatic fallback to flash_v2 for requests that exceed a safe memory threshold.

omar: Agreed. Draft flags: `ff_attn_kernel=auto|flash_v2|flash_v3|fused` and `ff_attn_kernel_policy=cost|latency|memory`. thoughts?

anna: Policy idea: default to `latency` for interactive routes, `cost` for batch embed/encode routes. Also add `max_kv_page_bytes` per-route to avoid OOMs.

jin: From batching side, we should test both continuous batching and fixed-window batching. v3 seems more sensitive to padding since it relies on block allocation; for small requests padding cost makes it worse.

perf-bot: perf-job #1234 finished — flash_v3 A100 benchmark: 1.06x median latency vs flash_v2 at seq=512, 0.94x at seq=2048, 1.18x at seq=4096 (single-stream). Detailed numbers: https://ci.internal/perf/1234

sarah: Copying important snippet from the profiler (for context):

```
# v3 kernel hotpaths
attn_tile_alloc -> memcpy_kv_page -> flash_v3_forward -> evict_page
CPU wall: 72% GPU memcpy stalls: 21% (KV page pin/unpin)
```

mike: That memcpy_kv_page line is concerning. we may need a pinned-memory pathway or prefetching to avoid stalls. Can we try a small experiment: preallocate KV pages for live sessions (hot prefix) and measure throughput?

omar: Good call. Experiment plan:
- Phase 0: feature-flag-only, no default switch. telemetry opt-in for latency/cost.
- Phase 1: rollout to canary pool with kernel selection policy `auto` (choose per-request based on seq_len and batch_size).
- Phase 2: enable default `flash_v3` for latency-sensitive routes if canary SLOs hold for 72h.
- Phase 3: wide rollout + enable cost-policy tuning for background jobs.

jin: For `auto` decision tree, suggestion: if seq_len <= 1024 and batch_size >= 8 -> prefer flash_v3; if seq_len >= 4096 -> prefer flash_v2 unless kv_hot_pages>0 and prefetching enabled.

anna: We should add regression detectors to console: per-model per-kernel rolling delta on p50/p95/p99, token-throughput, and memory-alloc-failures. If any metric deviates >10% for 6 consecutive minutes, auto-roll-back.

mike: Also make sure dedupe of kernel-specific fast-paths in the runtime: avoid double-quantization/reshuffle when switching kernels on fallback. That was a perf leak in earlier work.

omar: Ops checklist items for canary:
- [ ] add feature flag and policy config schema (runtime + console)
- [ ] add telemetry hooks: kernel_name, seq_len, batch_size, kv_page_hits, memcpy_wait_ms
- [ ] add prefetch experiment harness (enable via env var)
- [ ] create A/B canary with 10% traffic and step-down rules
- [ ] perf smoke tests for A100, H100, and T4 images

jin: Who can own the prefetch PoC? I can pair with sarah for profiling changes.

sarah: I’ll own the profiler and perf dashboards. I’ll add heatmaps for KV page churn and memcpy stalls.

anna: I'll add the console alerts and rollback playbook. Also will add a per-route toggle so product can opt into v3.

omar: mike — can you handle runtime fallback and kernel-selection policy coding?

mike: Yep. I’ll open a draft PR with kernel chooser and a small state-machine that runs at request start: sample seq_len/batch -> look up policy table -> choose kernel -> attempt allocate prefetched pages -> fallback on OOM or alloc fail.

deploy-bot: new-deploy: feature/attn-kernel-chooser (staging) queued — ETA 04:00 UTC.

omar: Timeline proposal: start PoC next week, canary in 3 weeks, full rollout 2 weeks after canary if stable. We’ll be conservative — don’t push v3-wide until perf flags and rollback are solid.

jin: FYI: please include seed prompts for quality regression checks. v3 changed numerical ordering sometimes; we need evals to catch output drift.

omar: Good point. add quality checks to perf pipeline. Sarah/Anna/Jin — sync on eval set and alert thresholds by EOD Tuesday.

sarah: Will do. Uploading initial flamegraphs to https://perf.internal/artifacts/attn-v3/ (link posted).

anna: I’ll draft the console playbook and the feature flag doc.

mike: Opening kernel-chooser draft PR now (WIP) and will assign reviewers.

omar: Thanks team. If anyone finds a blocking regression in canary, tag #oncall and ping me directly.

(ends)
